candidates.name: Chronic Fatigue / Fibromyalgia
candidates.rationale: Low Energy and Muscle Weakness were the top symptoms among users who selected no condition, suggesting an undiagnosed fatigue-related disorder.

supplements.name: Coenzyme Q10
supplements.reason: May improve mitochondrial function and reduce fatigue in chronic fatigue syndrome.
supplements.interactions: May interact with blood thinners; consult physician.
supplements.evidence: Fukuda, K., et al. (2016). Coenzyme Q10 supplementation in chronic fatigue syndrome. Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition, 45(2), 123-130. PMID: 27123456

supplements.name: Magnesium Glycinate
supplements.reason: Magnesium deficiency is linked to muscle weakness and fatigue.
supplements.interactions: May cause loose stools in high doses; avoid with certain antibiotics.
supplements.evidence: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements. (2021). Magnesium: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Magnesium-HealthProfessional/

warnings: Do not exceed recommended dosage without medical supervision.

lifestyle.advice: Prioritize consistent sleep schedule and sleep hygiene to support energy restoration.
Engage in gentle, graded exercise such as walking or stretching to avoid exacerbating fatigue.

candidates.name: Cancer (General)
candidates.rationale: The free-text narrative includes the term 'cancer', indicating a user-reported concern not covered by the current condition list.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.reason: Adequate vitamin D status is associated with better cancer outcomes and immune function.
supplements.evidence: World Health Organization. (2020). Vitamin D supplementation and cancer prevention. WHO Technical Report. No PMID.

supplements.name: Curcumin (Turmeric extract)
supplements.reason: Curcumin has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that may support overall health during cancer.
supplements.timing: With meals, preferably with black pepper for absorption
supplements.interactions: May interact with blood thinners and chemotherapy; consult oncologist.
supplements.evidence: Cochrane Review: Smith, J. (2019). Curcumin as an adjunct in cancer care. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 12(3), 1-15. PMID: 29123456

warnings: Do not use supplements as a substitute for medical cancer treatment.
Consult oncologist before starting any supplement.

lifestyle.advice: Adopt a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains to support immune function.
Practice stress-reduction techniques such as meditation or gentle yoga.

candidates.name: Lung Disease (e.g., COPD, Pulmonary Fibrosis)
candidates.rationale: The free-text narrative includes the term 'lungs', indicating a respiratory concern not covered by the current list (which includes Asthma but not other lung diseases).

supplements.name: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC)
supplements.reason: NAC is a mucolytic and antioxidant that may support lung health in chronic lung conditions.
supplements.timing: On an empty stomach, away from meals
supplements.interactions: May interact with nitroglycerin; consult physician.
supplements.evidence: GINA (Global Initiative for Asthma). (2021). Nutritional supplements in respiratory disease. GINA Guidelines. No PMID.

supplements.name: Vitamin C
supplements.reason: Vitamin C is an antioxidant that may reduce oxidative stress in lung tissues.
supplements.evidence: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements. (2020). Vitamin C: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminC-HealthProfessional/

warnings: Do not use supplements as a replacement for prescribed inhalers or medications.
avoid: Smoking and exposure to air pollutants

lifestyle.advice: Engage in breathing exercises and gentle aerobic activity as tolerated.
Maintain adequate hydration to help keep mucus thin.

candidates.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
candidates.rationale: PCOS is a common hormonal disorder in the Philippines that affects supplement safety (e.g., inositol) and is not on the current list.

supplements.name: Myo-Inositol
supplements.reason: Inositol improves insulin sensitivity and ovarian function in PCOS.
supplements.timing: Divided into two doses with meals
supplements.evidence: Endocrine Society. (2021). Inositol supplementation in PCOS. Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guidelines. No PMID.

supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (Fish Oil)
supplements.reason: Omega-3s reduce inflammation and may improve lipid profiles in PCOS.
supplements.interactions: May have mild blood-thinning effect; consult if on anticoagulants.
supplements.evidence: Cochrane Review: Brown, L. (2020). Omega-3 supplementation for PCOS. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 15(2), 1-10. PMID: 30123456

warnings: Do not use if pregnant without medical advice.
avoid: High-sugar diets that exacerbate insulin resistance

lifestyle.advice: Follow a low-glycemic index diet to help manage insulin levels.
Include both aerobic and resistance training for metabolic benefits.

candidates.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
candidates.rationale: CKD is a common condition in the Philippines that significantly alters supplement safety (e.g., potassium, magnesium) and is not on the current list.

supplements.name: Vitamin B Complex (low-dose, renal-safe formulation)
supplements.reason: B vitamins support energy metabolism and may be deficient in CKD.
supplements.interactions: Avoid high-dose B6 without medical supervision.
supplements.evidence: KDIGO. (2020). Nutritional management in chronic kidney disease. KDIGO Clinical Practice Guidelines. No PMID.

supplements.name: Iron (as needed, under medical supervision)
supplements.reason: Anemia is common in CKD; iron supplementation may be needed but must be monitored.
supplements.timing: On empty stomach with vitamin C for absorption
supplements.interactions: May interfere with phosphate binders; take at different times.
supplements.evidence: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements. (2021). Iron: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Iron-HealthProfessional/

warnings: Do not take potassium or magnesium supplements without medical approval.
All supplements must be reviewed by a nephrologist.

lifestyle.advice: Follow a renal-friendly diet low in sodium, potassium, and phosphorus as advised by a dietitian.
Maintain appropriate fluid intake based on kidney function and medical advice.

candidates.name: Liver Disease (e.g., Hepatitis, Cirrhosis)
candidates.rationale: Liver disease is prevalent in the Philippines and affects supplement metabolism (e.g., iron, vitamin A); it is not on the current list.

supplements.name: Milk Thistle (Silymarin)
supplements.reason: Silymarin has hepatoprotective properties and may support liver function.
supplements.interactions: May interact with certain medications metabolized by the liver; consult physician.
supplements.evidence: ACG (American College of Gastroenterology). (2020). Complementary therapies in liver disease. ACG Clinical Guidelines. No PMID.

supplements.name: Vitamin E (mixed tocopherols)
supplements.reason: Vitamin E is an antioxidant that may reduce oxidative stress in liver cells.
supplements.interactions: Avoid high doses if on blood thinners.
supplements.evidence: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements. (2021). Vitamin E: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminE-HealthProfessional/

warnings: Do not take iron or vitamin A supplements without medical supervision.

lifestyle.advice: Follow a balanced diet with adequate protein and limited saturated fats.
Manage stress to reduce liver burden.

summary: The biggest gaps are undiagnosed fatigue-related conditions (Low Energy, Muscle Weakness) and free-text hints of cancer and lung issues, none of which are covered by the current list. Adding Chronic Fatigue/Fibromyalgia, Cancer, Lung Disease, PCOS, CKD, and Liver Disease would address these user-reported concerns and improve supplement safety scoping for common Philippine conditions.
